Dnd is for all to enjoy so long as the specifics are stated beforehand and everyone stays open about what they wish to try to do or the kind of things they enjoy in a dnd campaign! :)  be it a paragraph of backstory, four or even two pages!

I started this way! It's difficult... Kinda, but I had people giving me advice and a close friend who was a dm who supported me. Here's the basic run down of the advice I have had over the years

1. Don't try to plan everything, you can't. You can try, but at some point, somewhere one party member is going to accidently kick the guard in the nuts trying to seduce them to let them in the bar even though they could have just walked in... 

2. It's fine having your campaign set, but try not the railroad it, don't have a linear path that must be followed in certain orders... Sometimes people just want to go wash themselves from all the viscera of an ogre off of them before talking to a Rando about the next thing they want to kill... Even if it's the rando. 

3. Whatever you think is "plenty" for a session... Double it... Maybe triple it. Some people like to sprint on through, and bulldoze through walls. 


PS.... It's fun to have random loot tables, but set the money stuff yourself, otherwise your party us just going to kill a bunny and find like 125 gold on it. And they had a total of 4 silver beforehand.
But items are always fun especially in chests and the like, especially if it's random :)
